title: 2007 AMC 10A 18
statement: Consider the \(12\)-sided polygon \(ABCDEFGHIJKL,\) as shown. Each of its sides has length \(4,\) and each two consecutive sides form a right angle. Suppose that \(\overline{AG}\) and \(\overline{CH}\) meet at \(M.\) What is the area of quadrilateral \(ABCM?\)

solutions.text:
Put the figure on coordinates with \(A = (-2, 6),\) \(B = (2, 6),\) \(C = (2, 2),\) \(G = (2, -6),\) and \(H = (-2, -6).\)

Line \(AG\) is \(y = -3x,\) and line \(CH\) is \(y = 2x - 2.\)

Their intersection is \(M = \left(\tfrac25, -\tfrac65\right).\)

Applying the shoelace formula to \(A, B, C, M\) gives \[ \begin{aligned} [ABCM] &=\dfrac12\left|{-8}-\dfrac{136}{5}\right|\\ &=\dfrac{88}{5}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Place the cross on coordinates using the side length \(4\)
Find \(M\) as the intersection of lines \(AG\) and \(CH,\) then apply the shoelace formula to \(ABCM\)
